name: OmniLisp Interpreter
target_user: systems programmers and compiler engineers studying functional evaluation models
problem: Standard scripting interpreters hide lexical closures, garbage collection roots, and evaluation environments behind heavy abstractions.
pain: Difficulty studying pure functional evaluation, proper tail recursion optimization (TRO), and custom mark-and-sweep memory management without relying on external runtime libraries.
solution: A zero-dependency Lisp interpreter and compiler implemented in C11. It features a custom S-expression lexer, recursive-descent parser, dynamic tagged-union object model, heap allocator with mark-and-sweep garbage collection, lexical environment chain resolver, Tail Call Optimization (TCO) evaluation loop, macro expansion engine, and interactive REPL environment.
verification: Comprehensive test suite verifying macro expansion hygiene, tail-call recursion depth stability without stack overflow, mark-and-sweep memory reclamation under induced heap pressure, and syntactic error recovery on malformed parenthetical inputs.
major_features: Custom S-expression lexer and recursive-descent parser producing an explicit Abstract Syntax Tree
Dynamic tagged-union object model representing symbols, lists, numbers, booleans, and primitive procedures
Lexical environment chain resolver supporting nested lexical scopes and closure capture
Tail Call Optimization (TCO) evaluation engine converting tail-recursive loops into constant-space iterations
Heap allocator and custom mark-and-sweep garbage collector tracking root sets and reclaiming unreferenced cells
Macro expansion engine supporting syntactic abstraction and hygienic code transformation
Built-in primitive procedure bindings for core arithmetic, logical comparisons, and list manipulation
Interactive Read-Eval-Print Loop (REPL) featuring multi-line input buffering and diagnostic error formatting
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
